items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: when he led his own band or fronted Luis Russell’s band in the thirties

ctx.x: I want to ask you a thing about him. They say that when Louis Armstrong took a solo it seemingly always had this wonderful finished quality. It wasn’t as if he rambled or was hunting for notes. It’s like when he got to the end it almost had this feeling of almost inevitable correctness.

Well I think a lot of the players then, once they got a certain chorus, remember in-person I don’t know how long they played, but I think I tend to believe that other than at jam sessions, the live performances were a lot like the recordings, you know, just a couple of choruses. Maybe they stretched a little bit more, but I think once they got a chorus they liked, they kind of stayed with that. Now we have alternate takes of things he’s done and they do vary, but they always have certain elements in them, you…
Tracing the lineage from that, from that trumpet player to another all-time favorite of mine, tell us what you know about Dizzy.
